text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when its motor neuron stops firing, so acetylcholine is cleared from the neuromuscular junction and the fibre is no longer excited. SERCA then pumps calcium back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and tropomyosin re-blocks the myosin-binding sites on actin. The shared note about a built-in intensity cutoff is not standard physiology (fibres respond all-or-none), so I haven't relied on it.

CONFIDENCE: 80
